phoneticConvention: Approximate English respelling for English-speaking readers (CAPITALS = stressed syllable; vowels ah / eh / ee / oh / oo; j and g before e/i → kh as in Scottish 'loch'; ñ → ny; ll → y; c before e/i and z → s; r is rolled; monosyllables in capitals). Standard Castilian with seseo and yeísmo. No substitute for the audio.
reviewStatus: Written by rule from validated content; native English review recommended.
title: Holding a conversation
goal: Hold a conversation mixing narrative, opinion, argument and clarification.

units.situation: Clarifying what the other person means

model.note: 'O sea' is very common in speech for rephrasing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¡Hola! ¿Qué tal el viaje a Portugal?
turns.phon: OH-lah. KEH TAHL EHL VEEAH-kheh AH pohr-too-GAHL
turns.native: Hi! How was the trip to Portugal?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: ¡Genial! Cuando llegamos a Lisboa, me puse muy contento.
turns.phon: kheh-NEEAHL. KOOAHN-doh yeh-GAH-mohs AH lees-BOH-ah, MEH POO-seh MOOEE kohn-TEHN-toh
turns.native: Great! When we arrived in Lisbon, I was so happy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Qué fue lo que más te gustó?
turns.phon: KEH FOOEH LOH KEH MAHS TEH goos-TOH
turns.native: What did you like most?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Lo que más me gustó fue la gente. Y la comida, claro.
turns.phon: LOH KEH MAHS MEH goos-TOH FOOEH LAH KHEHN-teh. EE LAH koh-MEE-dah, KLAH-roh
turns.native: What I liked most was the people. And the food, of course.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Y el tiempo? Yo creo que en octubre llueve mucho.
turns.phon: EE EHL TEEEHM-poh. YOH KREH-oh KEH EHN ohk-TOO-breh YOOEH-veh MOO-choh
turns.native: And the weather? I think it rains a lot in October.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Es verdad, pero solo llovió un día. Después hizo sol.
turns.phon: EHS vehr-DAHD, PEH-roh SOH-loh yoh-VEEOH OON DEE-ah. dehs-POOEHS EE-soh SOHL
turns.native: That's true, but it only rained one day. After that it was sunny.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¡Qué suerte! A mí me parece que Portugal es más barato que España.
turns.phon: KEH SOOEHR-teh. AH MEE MEH pah-REH-seh KEH pohr-too-GAHL EHS MAHS bah-RAH-toh KEH ehs-PAH-nyah
turns.native: Lucky you! Personally, I think Portugal is cheaper than Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Depende. Lisboa es más cara que antes.
turns.phon: deh-PEHN-deh. lees-BOH-ah EHS MAHS KAH-rah KEH AHN-tehs
turns.native: It depends. Lisbon is more expensive than before.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: O sea, que vale la pena ir, ¿no?
turns.phon: OH SEH-ah, KEH VAH-leh LAH PEH-nah EER, NOH
turns.native: So it's worth going, right?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Sí, sin duda. Al final fue una buena decisión.
turns.phon: SEE, SEEN DOO-dah. AHL fee-NAHL FOOEH OO-nah BOOEH-nah deh-see-SEEOHN
turns.native: Yes, definitely. In the end it was a good decision.

turns.study: Me han ofrecido un trabajo en Madrid. No sé qué hacer.

turns.phon: MAHS BEEEHN MEH DAH PEH-nah deh-KHAHR AH MEES ah-MEE-gohs
turns.native: It's more that I'm sad to leave my friends.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Es verdad, pero también hay ventajas: la ciudad es grande y hay más oportunidades.
turns.phon: EHS vehr-DAHD, PEH-roh tahm-BEEEHN AHEE vehn-TAH-khahs, LAH seeoo-DAHD EHS GRAHN-deh EE AHEE MAHS oh-pohr-too-nee-DAH-dehs
turns.native: That's true, but there are advantages too: the city is big and there are more opportunities.

turns.study: Tienes razón. Estoy de acuerdo con eso.

turns.native: You're right. I agree with that.

turns.study: A mí me parece que deberías aceptar. Si no te gusta, siempre puedes volver.

turns.native: Personally, I think you should accept. If you don't like it, you can always come back.

turns.study: En resumen, acepto y lo probamos. Gracias por escucharme.
turns.phon: EHN reh-SOO-mehn, ah-SEHP-toh EE LOH proh-BAH-mohs. GRAH-seeahs POHR ehs-koo-CHAHR-meh
turns.native: In short, I'll accept and we'll give it a try. Thanks for listening to me.

readiness: Hold a long conversation: tell a story with time markers and emotions, weigh up pros and cons, concede and then counter, rephrase the other person's view, sum up, change the subject and say a warm goodbye.
